$note: Career progression. Every number a designer would want to balance is here: what a match is worth, how steep the level curve is, what each skill rank does, and what unlocks an achievement. Nothing in this file can make a level unwinnable - the skills only ever help, and they default to zero, so a level-1 career plays the base game exactly as T.balance() measures it.

xp.$note: Awarded on a goal only. A miss costs nothing but the attempt.

level.$note: Total XP to REACH a level: base * (n-1)^exponent. A full 15-match career at three stars lands around level 8, so the curve still has room for replay.

skills.$note: All four act when the kick is constructed or when a level starts - never inside the simulation - so the physics and the keeper are untouched and balance testing stays honest.

power.name: POWER
power.desc: Two per cent more pace on every strike, per rank.

curve.name: CURVE
curve.desc: Six per cent more bend on the same stroke, per rank.

vision.name: VISION
vision.desc: A wider window to pick out a team-mate, per rank.

composure.name: COMPOSURE
composure.desc: An extra rewind every two ranks.

achievements.name: PERFECTIONIST
achievements.desc: Take all three stars in a match.

achievements.name: NERVELESS
achievements.desc: Win five matches without a rewind.

achievements.name: AROUND THE WALL
achievements.desc: Score with bend on the ball.

achievements.name: IN FORM
achievements.desc: Score in five matches in a row.
